newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - June 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in two London-based Arabic-language newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Qatar's Emir talks with U.S. president show differences over U.S. policy in Iraq and Iran.
- Signs of improvement in Egyptian-Iranian relations. Foreign ministers of both countries are due to meet in Istanbul on Saturday.
- U.S. banks and companies to finance setting up a refinery in Yemen at a cost of between $800 million and $1.2 billion.
- Tunisia needs $42 billion to carry out its 1997-2001 development plan.
- Kuwaiti parliament members urge the government to resign instead of dissolving parliament.
- Kuwait airline strike ends after negotiations.
- Resumption of Syrian trade with Iraq helps ease recession.
- Dubai emirate in the United Arab Emirates imported 350 tonnes of gold in 1996.
